text: When Satan quoted Psalm 91, he left out "to keep you in all your ways." God's protection is for your daily walk.
explanation:
The only time the devil quotes Scripture, he takes it from Psalm 91, and he misquotes it. "He shall give His angels charge over you, to keep you in all your ways. In their hands they shall bear you up, lest you dash your foot against a stone." He dropped the part about your ways and tried to turn a promise for walking into a dare to jump.

The picture is of an ordinary day: you're walking along, you don't see the rock in your path, and angels lift you over it without you noticing. You don't have to test God with foolish leaps, and you don't have to hide at home either. Walk your normal way, trusting Him; He keeps you in all of it.

text: God makes sure the enemy is under your feet, not over your head. Just keep walking.
explanation:
"Behold, I give you the authority to trample on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall by any means hurt you." You can't trample while sitting at home. Trampling happens as you go about your life, often without even seeing the danger.

So don't be devil-conscious. Walk with the Lord, and if the enemy gets in your way, he ends up underfoot. And "by any means" is a strong double negative in the Greek: by no means whatsoever. Disease, accident, tragedy: whatever route he tries, nothing shall by any means hurt you.

text: A traffic officer raises one hand and a loaded truck stops. Authority is greater than power.
explanation:
Jesus says He's given you authority "over all the power of the enemy." The enemy has power; don't deny it. But picture a heavy container truck at a junction and one officer raising his hand. The truck has far more power than the man, yet it comes to a complete stop.

It isn't about the officer's size or strength. It's who stands behind him: the government, the police, the whole nation. Behind your raised hand stands the risen Christ and the throne of heaven. You don't have to out-muscle the enemy. You only have to use the authority you've been given.

text: Thank God for the sickness that never reached you. He's protected you far more than you know.
explanation:
We thank God when He heals us, because we can see the before and after. But what about the illness the enemy had your name on that never arrived? The accident that missed you by a hair's breadth? The virus that was on its way to you and was turned back?

God is so often under-thanked while we're over-complaining. We fret over the 2% of the body that hurts and forget the 98% that works. "The Lord will take away from you all sickness." Start thanking Him for what He's kept away, not only for what He's taken away.

text: Even with Jesus beside them, the disciples "anointed with oil many who were sick, and healed them."
explanation:
Some think anointing oil is an Old Testament relic or a superstition. Yet in the New Testament, the disciples anointed the sick with oil and they were healed. And after Jesus ascended, James wrote to the church: "Is anyone among you sick? Let him call for the elders… anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord. And the prayer of faith will save the sick."

It isn't the oil; it's the Holy Spirit it represents, and faith in Him. Naaman thought dipping in the Jordan was ridiculous, but on the seventh time his flesh became like a child's. Strange instructions, powerful results. You can anoint yourself, your children, your home, your car. Oil is just oil, until God's anointing comes on it.

text: The first time oil appears in the Bible, Jacob pours it on a stone and calls the place Bethel: the house of God.
explanation:
Jacob had just deceived his father and cheated his brother. He was running for his life and slept with a stone for a pillow. Yet God met him in a dream with nothing but unconditional promises: "I am with you and will keep you wherever you go." Jacob woke and said, "How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of God," and poured oil on the stone.

The first mention of oil ties the anointing to the house of God. And Psalm 91 says, "Because you have made the Lord… your dwelling place, no evil shall befall you, nor shall any plague come near your dwelling." The house of God today isn't a building; it's His people gathered together. That's where the anointing flows.

text: Olives aren't oil until they're crushed. In Gethsemane, the "oil press," Jesus was crushed for you.
explanation:
Gethsemane means oil press. In Jesus' day, the first pressing of the olives gave oil for the temple lamps: He was crushed in the dark garden to bring light into our darkness. The second pressing was used for medicine: His back was torn by the scourge, and "by His stripes we are healed." The third pressing made soap: at the cross He was crushed under our judgment, and we are washed clean.

Bread doesn't grow in a wheat field, and wine doesn't hang on the vine. Grain must be ground and baked; grapes must be trodden. Every drop of the anointing, every blessing, came from Jesus being crushed in your place. That's how much He loves you.
